claim: WSL2 runs a Microsoft-built Linux kernel with full syscall compatibility and systemd, but performance across OS file systems is worse than WSL1; serial ports unsupported; kernel serviced by Windows Update.
quote: The Linux kernel in WSL 2 is built by Microsoft from the latest stable branch... The kernel will be serviced by Windows updates... WSL 2 does not include support for accessing serial ports.

claim: The WSL2 kernel repo's current default branch is linux-msft-wsl-6.18.y.
quote: linux-msft-wsl-6.18.y

claim: Reference for .wslconfig and wsl.conf options: systemd boot flag, memory/processors, networkingMode values, autoMemoryReclaim default dropCache, sparseVhd, defaultVhdSize 1TB, hostAddressLoopback/ignoredPorts require mirrored mode, and the 8-second config-reload rule.
quote: If the value is `dropCache` or an unknown value, cached memory will be reclaimed immediately. ... `defaultVhdSize` | size | `1099511627776` (1 TB) ... You must wait until the subsystem running your Linux distribution completely stops running and restarts for configuration setting updates to appear.

claim: Microsoft recommends against working across operating systems and says to store project files in the WSL (Linux) file system rather than /mnt/c.
quote: We recommend against working across operating systems with your files, unless you have a specific reason for doing so. For the fastest performance speed, store your files in the WSL file system if you are working in a Linux command line

claim: Measured filesystem throughput/IOPS for WSL native ext4 vs WSL to /mnt/c vs Windows to \\wsl$, showing 10-90% loss across the boundary.
quote: Windows→WSL writes are catastrophically slow (<1% performance)

claim: systemd support requires WSL 0.67.6+ and is enabled with [boot] systemd=true in /etc/wsl.conf followed by wsl.exe --shutdown.
quote: You'll need to be on version 0.67.6+ to have systemd support.

claim: WSL Containers (wslc) entered public preview on 29 June 2026 as part of WSL 2.9.3, with GA targeted for autumn 2026.
quote: WSL Containers brings a native Linux container experience to WSL for building, running, and managing of Linux containers via the wslc command line tool.

claim: Visual Studio provides a WSL launch profile for debugging .NET apps on Linux without a separate VM or container.
quote: Starting in Visual Studio 2019 version 16.11, the WSL 2 debug target was renamed to WSL.

claim: NVIDIA supports CUDA workloads inside WSL2 using the Windows host driver via GPU paravirtualization.
quote: NVIDIA GPU Accelerated Computing on WSL 2

claim: GPU access in WSL2 goes through /dev/dxg with stub libraries in /usr/lib/wsl/lib; installing a Linux GPU driver overrides the symlinks and breaks CUDA passthrough.
quote: The CUDA driver installed on Windows host will be stubbed, or sym linked/mapped, inside the VM as libcuda.so, and any Linux GPU driver will override the symlink and passthrough with CUDA will not work.

claim: WSLg provides Wayland and X11 support via Weston with an RDP backend, PulseAudio audio, and GPU acceleration through Mesa's d3d12 Gallium driver, remoting individual application windows.
quote: the rendered data is copied from VRAM to system memory before being presented to the compositor within WSLg, and uploaded onto the GPU again on the Windows side

claim: Phoronix benchmarked Ubuntu 24.04 under WSL2 on Windows 11 Pro 25H2 against bare-metal Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS on a Ryzen 9 9950X3D with 32GB RAM and a PCIe Gen5 NVMe SSD, published 15 September 2025.
quote: In effect, the current performance overhead/costs of using Windows Subsystem for Linux under Windows 11 rather than just booting to Ubuntu Linux directly.

claim: WSL2 on Windows 11 25H2 shows roughly 10-15% CPU overhead and up to 20% on I/O versus bare-metal Ubuntu, reaching 85-95% of native performance in many tests.
quote: WSL2 on Windows 11 25H2 incurs 10-15% overhead in CPU tasks and up to 20% in I/O compared to bare-metal Ubuntu.

claim: WSL was open sourced at Microsoft Build on 19 May 2025.
quote: The code that powers WSL is now available on GitHub at Microsoft/WSL and open sourced to the community.

claim: Open-sourced WSL components are wsl.exe, wslservice.exe, the Linux init/gns/localhost daemons and the plan9 server; lxcore.sys, p9rdr.sys and p9np.dll remain closed.
quote: The following components are still part of the Windows image and are not open sourced at this time: `Lxcore.sys`: the kernel side driver that powers WSL 1; `P9rdr.sys` and `p9np.dll`: The components which run the `\\wsl.localhost` filesystem redirection

claim: The official WSL source repository on GitHub.
quote: run your Linux command-line tools, utilities and applications, all unmodified and directly on Windows without the overhead of a traditional virtual machine or dual boot setup

claim: Windows drives are exposed to WSL2 by a plan9 file server started by wslservice.exe; mount.drvfs can alternatively use virtio-plan9 or virtiofs depending on .wslconfig.
quote: mount the drive as `drvfs` (WSL1), or `plan9`, `virtio-plan9` or `virtiofs` (WSL), depending on .wslconfig

claim: Long-standing open issue reporting WSL2 /mnt write throughput of 40.4 MB/s versus 442 MB/s under WSL1 on the same hardware.
quote: [wsl2] filesystem performance is much slower than wsl1 in /mnt

claim: virtiofs is enabled with virtiofs=true under [wsl2] and requires kernel 6.18.26.3-1 or newer; a PR merged 27 May 2026 gave each virtio device its own DMA pool, and plan9 remains the default.
quote: The per-device pool removes one of the remaining contention points on the virtiofs path.

claim: Hacker News discussion of WSL2's faster Windows file access reports a Hugo build at 50s on native WSL filesystem, 75s via virtiofs, versus an estimated 3-5 minutes on plan9.
quote: 50 seconds on the native WSL filesystem versus 75 seconds using virtiofs

claim: Dropbox and Google Drive cannot selectively ignore node_modules, making syncing of dependency trees extremely slow for repos inside synced folders.
quote: There is no way to not sync certain folders in Dropbox, which is a bigger problem with node_modules since syncing thousands of files is ridiculously slow.

claim: WSLg remotes individual windows rather than a whole desktop, so running a full DE requires XRDP; GNOME Shell needs 3D acceleration XRDP cannot provide and KDE Plasma 6.8 is Wayland-only.
quote: full desktop environments don't work well with WSLg since it remotes individual windows, not entire desktops

claim: Running a full desktop shell inside WSL2 requires a community workaround rather than a supported configuration.
quote: Full desktop shell in WSL2 using WSLg (XWayland)

claim: WSL2 clock skew occurs because the WSL VM's clock is not updated when the Windows host resumes from sleep or hibernate; the fix is sudo hwclock -s or a Kernel-Power triggered scheduled task.
quote: the clock skew happens when the host machine sleeps/hibernates because the VM for the WSL Linux distro doesn't have its clock updated when the host resumes

claim: USB device support in WSL2 is not native and requires the usbipd-win project, attaching devices by bus ID; while attached the device cannot be used by Windows.
quote: Support for connecting USB devices is not natively available in WSL, so you will need to install the open-source usbipd-win project. ... as long as the USB device is attached to WSL, it cannot be used by Windows.

claim: usbipd-win is the USB/IP implementation used to attach Windows USB devices to WSL2.
quote: Windows software for sharing locally connected USB devices to other machines, including Hyper-V guests and WSL 2.

claim: WSL2 defaults to NAT with its own virtualized ethernet adapter and a changing IP, requiring netsh portproxy for LAN access; mirrored mode requires Windows 11 22H2+ and does not support the IPv6 localhost address ::1.
quote: WSL 2 has a virtualized ethernet adapter with its own unique IP address. ... Connect to Windows servers from within Linux using the localhost address `127.0.0.1`. IPv6 localhost address `::1` is not supported

claim: Mirrored networking silently falls back to NAT on Windows builds that lack the required features.
quote: wsl: Mirrored networking mode is not supported: Windows version 26100.4202 does not have the required features. Falling back to NAT networking.

claim: snapd does not work inside WSL, a limitation open for years.
quote: snapd does not work inside WSL

claim: systemd 256 and later require plain cgroup v2 support, which WSL's hybrid cgroup v1 hierarchy did not provide.
quote: systemd >= 256 needs plain cgroupv2 support

claim: WSL2 memory grows because the Linux page cache balloons; Microsoft's example shows 2 GB attributed to the VM on Windows while Linux in-use memory is only 50 MB.
quote: when the memory needs of the WSL2 Virtual Machine (VM) would grow, either from your workflow or by the Linux kernel, the overall memory allocated to the VM would also grow by allocating more memory from the host

claim: The WSL2 ext4.vhdx grows but never shrinks when files are deleted; reclaiming space needs fstrim plus Optimize-VHD, or sparse mode.
quote: WSL2 virtual disks grow but never shrink on their own.

claim: Once a WSL VHD is sparse, Optimize-VHD refuses to compact it, so manual compaction is no longer available.
quote: Virtual hard disk files must be uncompressed and unencrypted and must not be sparse.

claim: inotify events do not fire for files on Windows-mounted paths in WSL2, breaking hot reload and file watchers; polling is the workaround.
quote: INotify for mounted folders does not work with WSL2, and when editing source found in mounted folders the watch logic never triggers.

claim: NTFS drives mounted in WSL are case-insensitive by default (case=off) while ext4 is case-sensitive; mixed-case files become inaccessible to Windows applications and git core.ignorecase must be set to match.
quote: Default setting: `off` for case sensitivity unavailable (all directories on mounted NTFS drives will be case insensitive). ... Setting this option to false on a case-insensitive file system may lead to confusing errors, false conflicts, or duplicate files.

claim: WSL added per-distro cgroup isolation for systemd instances, with an IsolateDistroCgroup .wslconfig option defaulting to true.
quote: Protect critical WSL processes under heavy load with cgroup & isolate distro cgroups

claim: The redesigned WSL resource management relies entirely on cgroup v2, breaking legacy cgroup v1 workloads unless IsolateDistroCgroup is set to false.
quote: A .wslconfig option IsolateDistroCgroup (default true) is added so users can opt-out of this and keep using cgroup v1.

claim: The right moment to move from WSL2 to dual boot is when the frustration stops being about Linux commands and becomes about wanting Linux to be the whole experience; WSL2 mistakes are easier to unwind than dual-boot mistakes.
quote: The right time to transition to dual boot usually arrives when frustration is no longer about learning Linux commands and starts becoming about wanting Linux to be the whole experience
